note:
The link-detection table (CANT-329, under CANT-308). ONE definition of which URL in a draft a link preview is asked about, read by the web test (web/linkpreview.test.ts), the Dart client's (dart-client/test/link_preview_test.dart) and the Flutter app's (app/test/link_preview_test.dart). Nothing else defines it; a client that disagrees with a row here is the client that is wrong.

The rule, as the CANT-308 plan pins it and the clients build it:
  1. A token is `http://` or `https://` (the scheme is case-sensitive, lower case only) immediately followed by one or more non-whitespace characters. The first such token in the text is the candidate. A bare scheme followed by whitespace or the end of the text is not a token: it is a URL still being typed.
  2. Trailing `.` `,` `;` `:` `!` `?` `)` are trimmed, repeatedly. Nothing else is: a quote, `>` or `]` stays, and a URL that legitimately ends in `)` loses it. The rule is a pinned approximation and is not trying to parse prose.
  3. If nothing is left after the scheme, there is no URL. The scan does not go on to a later token.
  4. `ask` is whether a preview is requested for it: the host must contain a dot and not end with one. A draft with a URL that is not askable still has that URL (the composer holds it) but sends no request. The idle time before the request is 600 ms and is a constant in each client, not a row here.

Each case: `name` (unique), `text` (the draft), `url` (the detected URL, or null), `ask` (boolean; false whenever `url` is null).

This file is hand-written and is the source: it is not generated, and every runner reads it. A hand edit that makes a client disagree fails that client's test, and verify.sh also mutates each client's rule in turn and requires its test to fail.

cases.name: mid-sentence, query and fragment, comma after
query ending in a value, then punctuation
a closing parenthesis that belongs to the URL is trimmed
a closing quote is not trimmed
an angle bracket is not trimmed
two urls, the first wins, plain words
carriage return and line feed end the token
a no-break space ends the token
ftp before an http url is skipped
upper-case scheme before a lower-case url
host with no dot is detected but not asked
host with no dot, with a port
half-typed host is detected but not asked
a dot only in the path does not make a host
a bare scheme is not a token, so a later url is found
a token that trims to nothing ends the scan
